name: World-readable/writable file or preference mode
attack_scenario: A malicious app on the same device opens the victim's world-readable SharedPreferences file and reads the stored session token, or overwrites a world-writable config to point the app at an attacker server.
negative_test_hint: write the session token with "Context.MODE_WORLD_READABLE" and assert the call throws SecurityException or is rejected, never leaving the file readable by other apps

exemplar.noncompliant:
val prefs = getSharedPreferences("auth", Context.MODE_WORLD_READABLE)
openFileOutput("session.dat", Context.MODE_WORLD_WRITEABLE).use { it.write(token) }
exemplar.compliant:
val prefs = getSharedPreferences("auth", Context.MODE_PRIVATE)
openFileOutput("session.dat", Context.MODE_PRIVATE).use { it.write(token) }
exemplar.explanation: MODE_WORLD_READABLE/MODE_WORLD_WRITEABLE make the file or SharedPreferences readable/writable by every other app on the device, breaking the app sandbox. They were deprecated and throw SecurityException on API 24+, but legacy code still uses them and downgrades storage of tokens/PII to shared state. CWE-276 / OWASP MASVS-STORAGE.
